subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 2

text: Member, Board of Supervisors

The Board of Supervisors is the legislative branch of government for the City and County of San Francisco. It enacts local laws and adopts the City’s annual budget. There are eleven members, each elected to a four-year term. The current annual salary is $180,102. Voters in Districts 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 will vote for their member of the Board of Supervisors in this election.
Manager / Retired Military.
Retired Military
23-year resident of District 2
Former Federal law enforcement
Supports business, is business manager
Has been a target of crime, understands crime victims
NOT a politician or activist

I’m not a career politician making exaggerated accomplishment claims or hollow, meaningless support for what should automatically be basic values in our city. I’m a regular, hardworking, common-sense & believer in real solutions. Regardless who gets the credit. I’m not feeding an ego, nor seeing this as a step to higher office.
I’ll be the sensible Board member who’ll:
Force Homeless agencies to be more effective RESOLVING Homelessness instead of lining pockets.
Hold Homeless individuals REFUSING help accountable to the same laws we ALL follow.

Focus new housing creation towards working
San Franciscans at market rates and below INSTEAD of high-end housing.
Recognize businesses pay our bills. We need to do away with EXCESSIVE regulations & costs that impede small businesses opening and large businesses staying.
Encourage residents to take an active role in the city: If you see something wrong, report it. Expect what you accept.
Get repeat offenders and career criminals off the streets.
Vote Guy McCoy, District 2 Supervisor.

text: Community Advocate / Immigrant Rights Commissioner.

Monthanus Ratanapakdee is a longtime San Francisco resident for nearly three decades, community advocate, nonprofit founder, and public safety leader. She founded the Justice for Vicha Foundation after her father, Vicha Ratanapakdee, was killed in an unprovoked attack, helping bring national attention to anti-Asian hate, senior safety, and victims’ rights.

She serves on San Francisco’s Immigrant Rights Commission and has worked with residents, seniors, immigrants, families, victims, and small businesses across San Francisco. Her work focuses on public safety, accountability, neighborhood quality of life, language access, and community healing.

As an independent candidate for Supervisor, Monthanus is not backed by political party machines or big-money interests. She supports safer streets, cleaner neighborhoods, stronger support for small businesses, protecting the character of District 2 neighborhoods, responsible use of taxpayer dollars, compassionate policies with accountability, stronger protections for seniors and victims, and consequences for repeat violent offenders.
Monthanus believes San Francisco can be safe, compassionate, economically strong, and accountable to the people again.
